metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in White Mesa, UT | San Juan County
metaDescription: Own fee mineral rights near White Mesa, UT? We navigate the area's Ute trust land and uranium mill history and evaluate non-tribal interests honestly.
heroLead: White Mesa is a Ute Mountain Ute community south of Blanding, and it's also home to the last operating conventional uranium mill in the country, which makes mineral ownership here unusually layered.
intro: Most of the land at White Mesa itself is Ute Mountain Ute tribal trust land, which we don't purchase, but the surrounding stretch of southern San Juan County includes fee parcels held by non-tribal owners, some tied to ranching families, others to the uranium and vanadium interests that supplied the White Mesa Mill and its predecessors going back decades.

This is one of the more specialized corners of our coverage area, and we approach every inquiry here by first confirming ownership type, then figuring out which substances the deed actually covers, since uranium and conventional oil and gas trade in entirely different markets with different buyers.

sections.heading: Tribal trust land versus fee ownership
paragraphs: If your interest traces to a BIA allotment or tribal trust designation, we can't purchase it directly and would point you toward the appropriate tribal or BIA office. A standard recorded deed with the San Juan County recorder indicates fee ownership, which we can evaluate.
Send us whatever documentation you have and we'll confirm which category applies honestly before any discussion of value.

sections.heading: Uranium and vanadium versus oil and gas
paragraphs: The White Mesa Mill has processed uranium ore from mines across the region for decades, and some older San Juan County deeds in this area specifically reserve uranium and vanadium rights, separate from any conventional oil and gas potential. If your family's paperwork mentions these substances by name, that's a distinct asset with its own market and buyers.

Where a deed grants minerals broadly, any oil and gas potential ties back to the broader Paradox Basin, particularly the mature Aneth trend to the east, and we value that separately from uranium potential on the same tract.

sections.heading: What we need to get started
paragraphs: A recorded deed or probate document, a legal description, and any royalty or lease history are the starting point. We research the San Juan County recorder's records to confirm exactly what you hold and which substances are involved before making an offer, and there's no cost or obligation to find out.

faqs.question: Is the land at White Mesa itself tribal trust land?
faqs.answer: Most of it, yes, held by the Ute Mountain Ute Tribe. We don't purchase tribal trust or allotted interests, but fee parcels in the surrounding area of southern San Juan County are a different matter and something we can evaluate.

faqs.question: My deed mentions uranium and vanadium specifically. Is that the same as oil and gas rights?
faqs.answer: No, it's a distinct mineral category tied to the region's mining history and the nearby mill. We evaluate uranium and vanadium interests separately from any oil and gas potential on the same land.

faqs.question: How do I find out which category my interest falls into?
faqs.answer: Send us your deed or probate paperwork and we'll research it against San Juan County records and tell you plainly whether it's fee land, tribal trust land, and which substances it covers.
